issues.failure_explanation: The identity \(\langle \bar e_j, \mathbb I^*\mathbb I\bar e_j\rangle = \lambda_j^{-1}\langle \bar e_j, \Delta\mathbb I^*\mathbb I\bar e_j\rangle\) used to go from line 1 to line 2 is off by a factor of \(-1\): since \(\mathbb I^*\mathbb I\bar e_j = e_j\) on \(L^2_0\) and \(\Delta e_j = -\lambda_j e_j\), the correct relation is \(\langle\bar e_j,\mathbb I^*\mathbb I\bar e_j\rangle = -\lambda_j^{-1}\langle\bar e_j,\Delta\mathbb I^*\mathbb I\bar e_j\rangle\). This yields a negative expression \(\sum\lambda_j^{-a+1}\langle\mathcal I^{-1}e_j,e_j\rangle\) for \(E\|Z\|^2_{h^{-a}}\) (which must be positive), and the subsequent Cauchy-Schwarz bound \(\langle\mathcal I^{-1}e_j,e_j\rangle \le \|\cdot\|\|\cdot\|\) is trivially true (negative \(\le\) positive) and proves nothing.

issues.failure_explanation: Two interacting errors make the proof invalid. (1) The weak variance is bounded via Condition gemol B as \(\sigma_N^2 \lesssim \tilde\delta_N^2(\zeta)\), but the quadratic remainder from Condition gemol C gives the sharper \(\|g_{\theta,\psi}\|_{L^2(\mathcal X)} \lesssim \|\theta_{(t,\psi)}-\theta_0\|^2_{L^2}\), hence \(\sigma_N \lesssim \tilde\delta_N^2(0) \ll \tilde\delta_N(\zeta)\). With the suboptimal variance the first term of the Bernstein bound does not converge to zero. (2) The exponent computation \(\sqrt N\int_0^{\sigma_N}u^{-d/(2\beta)}du \lesssim \sqrt N\tilde\delta_N^{2-d/\beta}(\zeta)\) is wrong: the integral equals \(\Theta(\sigma_N^{1-d/(2\beta)}) = \Theta(\tilde\delta_N^{1-d/(2\beta)}(\zeta))\), and \(\tilde\delta_N^{2-d/\beta} = [\tilde\delta_N^{1-d/(2\beta)}]^2 < \tilde\delta_N^{1-d/(2\beta)}\) for \(\tilde\delta_N < 1\). The wrong exponent artificially deflates the bound, masking the insufficiency of the suboptimal variance.

issues.why_classification: The repair requires recognizing that the quadratic remainder from Condition gemol C provides a strictly stronger variance bound than Condition gemol B, then recomputing the Bernstein-type chaining bound with corrected exponents. issues.failure_explanation: The pointwise inequality \(\|a\|^2 \ge \|b\|^2 - \|a-b\|^2\) used at every time step is equivalent to \(\langle a, a-b\rangle \ge 0\), which is not true in general (e.g., take \(a = \tfrac12 b\)). Consequently the integral inequality \(\int\|U_h\|^2 \ge \int\|U_h^{(\varepsilon)}\|^2 - \int\|U_h - U_h^{(\varepsilon)}\|^2\) is false, and the entire lower-bound argument for \(\int_0^T\|U_h\|^2 ds\) fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false inequality with the standard bound \(\|a\|^2 \ge \tfrac12\|b\|^2 - \|a-b\|^2\) (from Young's inequality \(2\|b\|\|a-b\| \le \tfrac12\|b\|^2 + 2\|a-b\|^2\)). The conclusion is preserved: the main spectral lower bound for \(\int\|U_h^{(\varepsilon)}\|^2\) is halved and the error term is unchanged, so choosing \(\varepsilon\) sufficiently small still yields a positive constant \(c(M,T,d)\).
issues.overall_effect: Lemma paristexas (Lipschitz stability \(\int\|U_h\|^2 \ge c\|h\|_{H^{-1}}^2\)) is unproven. This lemma is the key input for Lemma injep0 (injectivity of \(\mathcal I\)), the stability Condition gemol E via (dochparis), and hence Theorem raf (Condition gemol F) and Theorems bvminv and ganzwien.
issues.title: False lower-bound inequality in proof of Lipschitz stability of parabolic flow
issues.why_classification: Replacing one inequality with a standard Young's-inequality bound and adjusting the numerical constant at the end is a short, local, routine repair. The method (compare with constant-potential approximation), conclusion (Lipschitz stability), rate, and scope all survive with no new lemma or replacement argument.

\mathbb I_\theta^* \mathbb I_\theta = \mathbb I_{\theta, \varepsilon}^* \mathbb I_{\theta, \varepsilon}  + \varepsilon K_2 = -\Delta^{-1} +K_{1,\varepsilon} +\varepsilon  K_2  ~~\text{any } \varepsilon>0,

issues.failure_explanation: The computation \(\int_0^{\varepsilon/4}\frac{\partial}{\partial t}U(2t,\cdot)\,dt\) is evaluated as \(U(\varepsilon/2)-h\), treating \(\frac{\partial}{\partial t}U(2t)\) as the derivative of \(t\mapsto U(2t)\). But the preceding identity \(\Delta U(2t) = \frac{\partial}{\partial t}U(2t) + WU(2t)\) requires \(\frac{\partial}{\partial t}U(2t) = U'(2t)\) (the time derivative of \(U\) at argument \(2t\)). The chain rule gives \(\int_0^{\varepsilon/4}U'(2t)\,dt = \tfrac12[U(\varepsilon/2)-h]\), not \(U(\varepsilon/2)-h\). Hence the correct identity is \(-\mathcal I_\varepsilon = \tfrac12\,Id + K_\varepsilon\), not \(-\mathcal I_\varepsilon = Id + K_\varepsilon\). The Fredholm argument and homeomorphism conclusion survive, but the specific decomposition \(\mathbb I^*\mathbb I \approx -\Delta^{-1}\) in Remark clever should read \(\mathbb I^*\mathbb I \approx -\tfrac12\Delta^{-1}\).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the chain-rule computation: \(\int_0^{\varepsilon/4}U'(2t)\,dt = \tfrac12[U(\varepsilon/2)-h]\). This yields \(-\mathcal I = \tfrac12\,Id + K'\), and the Fredholm argument proceeds after absorbing the scalar factor. Update Remark clever to read \(\mathbb I^*\mathbb I = -\tfrac12\Delta^{-1} + K_{1,\varepsilon} + \varepsilon K_2\).
issues.overall_effect: The claimed identity \(-\mathcal I = Id + K\) is wrong (it is \(-\mathcal I = \tfrac12\,Id + K'\)), but the Fredholm alternative argument works with any nonzero scalar multiple of the identity plus a compact operator, so Theorem raf's homeomorphism conclusion is preserved. The decomposition in Remark clever carries the wrong constant. No formal result is invalidated.
